title: Researching online
examples: How do I find good websites for my report?
When do I need to give credit for information?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to research things online.

items: Use quotation marks for exact phrases

explain.say: If you search for 'dinosaur teeth', you get too many results.
A reliable source has clear author names and dates.
Check if the website is from a school or a university.
When you use someone else's idea, you must cite it.
For example, if you read about photosynthesis, cite the book or page.

faq.q: How do I know if a website is biased?
faq.a: Bias means the source only shows one side of a story. Look for different viewpoints presented fairly.
asks: Does bias mean it is fake?
How can I spot unfair information?

faq.q: Should I use Wikipedia for my main facts?
faq.a: Wikipedia is a good starting point for ideas, but always find deeper information from expert sites.

faq.q: What is the difference between citing and paraphrasing?
faq.a: Paraphrasing means putting the idea into your own words. Citing means telling people where you got the idea.
asks: Do I need to change the words?
What is the rule for using other people's ideas?

faq.q: If I use an image, do I need to cite that too?
faq.a: Yes, you must cite images and any specific data you use, just like text.
asks: Where do I cite a photo?

faq.q: What if I can't find an author?
faq.a: If there is no author, try to find the organization that published the information instead.
asks: No name listed, what to do?
Who is responsible for the website?

facts: Always check the source's credentials before trusting information.
Using specific search terms narrows down too much information.
Citing sources gives credit to the original creators of ideas.
Look for .edu or .gov domains for academic or government sources.

quiz.say: Which search term combination is most likely to give specific results about the Roman Empire?
quiz.show: dinosaur teeth vs Roman Empire trade routes
quiz.why: This uses specific nouns and a clear relationship, making the search very focused.

wrong.1: This is too general and will bring up everything about teeth.
wrong.2: The order is unnatural and might confuse the search engine.
wrong.3: It misses the key geographical context of the Roman Empire.

quiz.say: If you use a statistic about global warming, you must:

options.show: Use a picture of the data.
options.say: Use a picture of the data.

options.show: Cite the source of the statistic.
options.say: Cite the source of the statistic.

quiz.why: Citing shows where you learned the number, which is academic honesty.

wrong.0: The picture itself must also be credited if you did not take it.
wrong.1: You need more detail than just the website name for proper citation.
wrong.3: Paraphrasing is not enough; you must credit the original data.
